summary: Swing sends mouse and keyboard events to listener objects that you add to a component. Each listener method changes your data and then calls repaint() to redraw.
notes: addMouseListener(new MouseAdapter() { ... }) adds an object, not a function. MouseAdapter and KeyAdapter supply empty versions of the methods you skip.
e.getKeyCode() returns constants like KeyEvent.VK_LEFT for the arrow keys.
repaint() does not draw right away. It asks Swing to call paintComponent soon.
pitfall: Forgetting setFocusable(true) or requestFocusInWindow() means keyPressed never runs. Mouse clicks still work, so the bug looks like broken arrow keys.
shot_note: After one click near the top left and three Right presses.
